deployed_sequence: Place both trays open-side up on a level table and engage the 2 mm lapped seam.
Slide both broad seam keys fully home from opposite sides; each has an end-stop shoulder and a raised comet-tail grip.

Drop each assembled gate bridge's T-feet through its station keyholes, slide the bridge 6 mm to the broad stop under the retaining shoulders, and confirm it cannot lift without reversing that motion; confirm each pendulum keeper is closed.

Move each pendulum gently by hand and confirm it clears the deck, crosses the raised center witness at least three times after a full-stop release, and returns to rest. If it rubs, sticks, cracks, crosses fewer than three times, or a bridge lifts, stop; the artifact has failed the setup check. Before every later pulse, both blades must again be at rest and both bridges fully seated.

Slide one dual-well magazine onto each external end-wall land. Stack six Sun-ridge comets flat in one READY well and six Orbit-ring comets flat in the opposite READY well; leave both SPENT wells empty. Solo uses either six-piece set in one READY well.

Read each vault by its recessed 2, 4, or 6 pips and locate the shooter's two eligible three-ridge facets in the target-end zone beyond that shooter's far gate. The two facets near the shooter's own end belong to the opposite shooting direction. No color knowledge is required.
assembly_and_tactile_setup.physical_encoding: The six arrow pairs are embossed around both removable READY/SPENT magazines in the same shooter-relative order. L/R is always from the current shooter's viewpoint. Each player receives the same pattern in a wave; the repeated final patterns are intended to permit within-match adaptation without extra cards, dice, or apps, PLAYTEST_VERIFY.
pulse_patterns: Wave 1: far gate left stop, then near gate left stop.
Wave 2: far right, then near right.
Wave 3: far left, then near right.
Wave 4: far right, then near left.
Wave 5: repeat far left, then near left.
Wave 6: repeat far right, then near right.

assumptions: A flat, level, rigid indoor table is available; table level meaningfully affects sliding and pendulum rest.
A consumer FFF printer can produce the 206 x 186 mm trays within the assumed 210 x 210 mm XY envelope, but actual usable bed area, origin exclusions, and brim requirements vary and must be checked.
A 30 mm x 5.5 mm printed disc can slide and bank repeatably enough on the printed deck for a skill game; this is unverified and may require surface/texture revision.
Two independently released pendulums remain visibly active long enough for one person to launch; this is the largest interaction assumption and must be tested early.
The 2/4/6 plus 2 scoring economy creates meaningful direct-versus-bank and vault risk choices; no balance or difficulty claim is made until Playtest.
All dimensions are nominal CAD values before printer/material compensation.

authority_and_claim_labels.design_decision: Dimensions, rules, forms, and target values below are deliberate starting design authority for Make unless explicitly marked provisional or superseded by a host-authorized downstream revision.
authority_and_claim_labels.researched_fact: Only claims explicitly bound to IDs in research.claim_bindings are treated as sourced facts.
authority_and_claim_labels.unverified: No print, physical fit, swing duration, bank response, safety certification, human enjoyment, balance, or difficulty result is claimed at Invent. Items marked MAKE_PHYSICAL_VERIFY or PLAYTEST_VERIFY remain unresolved.

comet_magazines.form: Two identical 72 x 38 x 8 mm flat bases, each with adjacent 32 mm diameter x 1.5 mm deep circular READY and SPENT wells. Six 5.5 mm comets stack flat to 33 mm nominal height in either well; the low rim registers the stack without hiding its height.
comet_magazines.placement_and_interface: One magazine slides sideways onto two 8 x 6 x 3 mm external dovetail tongues on each outer end wall with 0.30 mm nominal side clearance and a broad stop. Installed magazines extend 38 mm outward beyond each 410 mm field-body end for a 486 mm total deployed length and do not overlap the active deck. READY/SPENT words, a rising/falling relief, and the six pulse arrow pairs are embossed on the border.
comet_magazines.print_stance: Broad base on the build plate; no support intended. Magazine fit, six-disc stack stability, and finger removal are MAKE_PHYSICAL_VERIFY.

comets.form: Low circular sliding discs, 30 mm diameter x 5.5 mm high, with flat functional underside, 0.7 mm edge chamfers, and no pointed tail.
comets.interaction: Place one comet flat and wholly inside the active launch bay, then use one bare fingertip for one forward flick. There is no launcher, flexure, elastic, or stored-energy device.
comets.print_stance: Flat underside on the build plate. Make must verify bottom flatness, edge finish, mass consistency, and that relief does not invite stacking or alter sliding.
comets.tactile_sets: Six Sun-ridge discs carry one central raised sunburst no more than 0.8 mm high; six Orbit-ring discs carry two concentric raised rings no more than 0.8 mm high. The relief is intended to make ownership legible without color, PLAYTEST_VERIFY.

features: A 2.4 mm flat deck with no perimeter floor cove that could ramp a comet upward.
Side walls 20 mm above the deck and 2.8 mm thick, with a 2 mm inward retention lip whose underside is a 45-degree support-free chamfer.

A 2 mm lapped center seam plus two enlarged external side-wall seam bosses with horizontal chamfered slide-key lands above the deck plane; no lock track lies beneath the 2.4 mm floor. Top surfaces target coplanarity with a seam step no greater than 0.25 mm, MAKE_PHYSICAL_VERIFY.

Two full-width gate stations centered at common-field x=145 and x=245 after assembly. From either shooter's x=78 or x=312 witness line, these are respectively the near plane 67 mm downfield and the far plane 167 mm downfield. At each plane, integral left and right cheeks occupy y=0..32 and y=138..170, stand 8 mm above the deck, and are 6 mm thick along x with 1 mm rounded approach edges. The removable 110 mm bridge spans y=30..140, overlapping each cheek by 2 mm; its fixed legs cover y=30..43 and y=127..140, leaving only the bounded y=43..127 portal. Cheeks rise integrally from the deck with zero underside gap, so a 30 x 5.5 mm comet has no end or underpass route.

One clear launch bay at each end, 90 mm wide across y and 30 mm long downfield: x=48..78 for the left shooter and x=312..342 for the right shooter. Each bay begins 10 mm infield of its home vault scoring plane, so it does not overlap the 38 mm deep vault pockets.

Each outer end wall has two external non-flexural dovetail lands for a removable dual-well comet magazine. The left magazine extends behind the x=0 end and the right magazine is its 180-degree rotational mirror beyond x=390, keeping every supply piece outside the active field, vaults, rails, and bank facets.

Four designated 60 mm long bank facets total: a left/right rail pair spanning x=56..116 for shots toward the x=38 vault plane, and its 180-degree rotational mirror spanning x=274..334 for shots toward x=352. Thus each shooting direction has exactly two eligible target-end facets after its far gate. Each facet is angled 18 degrees inward and carries three raised diagonal ridges so bonus contact is visible and tactile without color.

Three integral vaults at each end, each 38 mm deep, separated by 2.8 mm walls, with a flush deck mouth and an embossed scoring plane at common-field x=38 or x=352. The field geometry must deny any route that bypasses a gate around its end.
field_trays.form: Two mirrored shallow trays, each nominally 206 x 186 x 20 mm, placed open-side up end-to-end with a 2 mm lapped seam for a 410 x 186 mm outer play body, and rim-to-rim for storage.
field_trays.interfaces: Tray A has the upper half of the 2 mm lap and Tray B the lower half. Two 46 x 12 x 4 mm flat keys slide horizontally across chamfered external side-wall seam lands, above and outside the active deck, with 0.30 mm nominal clearance per mating side. The same keys fit recessed exterior packed-lock lands when trays are rim-to-rim. Dimensions are starting values subject to Make fit coupons.
field_trays.print_stance: Deck bottom on the build plate, one tray per bed, no support intended.

gate_bridges.bearing: Two top-access open bearing seats accept the pendulum's integral 4.0 mm diameter trunnions. Seat diameter starts at 4.6 mm, with 0.3-0.4 mm axial clearance per side. A 28 x 10 x 3 mm sliding keeper closes both seats by geometric capture and has a 12 mm thumb tab; it is not a tiny hidden fastener.
gate_bridges.form: Two identical removable portal modules, each approximately 110 mm wide x 64 mm high x 14 mm deep. Fixed side cheeks complete a field-spanning barrier while the bridge provides an 84 mm wide clear portal divided by its moving blade.
gate_bridges.mounting: Two 12 x 18 mm keyed T-feet drop through enlarged station keyholes and then slide 6 mm downfield beneath 2.5 mm retaining shoulders to a broad hard stop, providing non-flexural geometric lift retention. Mating clearance starts at 0.25 mm per side. Asymmetric foot spacing makes backwards assembly visibly impossible; MAKE_PHYSICAL_VERIFY insertion force, impact retention, and wear.
gate_bridges.print_stance: Bridge lies on its broad rear face; keeper lies flat. No support intended.
gate_bridges.stops: Integral inspectable stops limit pendulum rotation to approximately plus or minus 50 degrees and prevent blade-to-frame impact. A raised center witness on the fixed bridge and a matching blade index make center crossings countable without color.

gravity_blades.form: A planar pendulum with a 6 mm wide x 4 mm thick arm, at least 3 mm root fillets, integral coaxial trunnions, and a rounded 14 mm wide x 12 mm tall x 8 mm deep lower paddle. No separate weight is used.
gravity_blades.geometry: Pivot is exactly 38 mm above the nominal deck and pivot-to-paddle center is 29 mm. The entire lower paddle contour is bounded by a 35 mm radius circular arc centered on the pivot, giving 3.0 mm nominal minimum deck clearance through the full rotation; a 5.5 mm comet therefore cannot pass under nominal geometry. With an 84 mm portal and 14 mm paddle, neutral left/right gaps are 35 mm. At the 50-degree stop, the paddle-center lateral displacement is about 22.2 mm, making one gap about 12.8 mm and the other about 57.2 mm. CAD must check the exact full swept solid and tolerance stack; these calculations are not fit or motion evidence.
gravity_blades.motion: The active player lifts each paddle to a marked left or right stop and releases it. Gravity returns it through center and it oscillates with decaying amplitude; gravity does not sustain continuous motion. Blade contact is live and may redirect the comet if the gate remains seated.
gravity_blades.print_stance: Broad blade face on the build plate with trunnions oriented vertically; no support intended. Trunnion layer strength and survival are MAKE_PHYSICAL_VERIFY.

seam_keys_and_storage_locks.form: Two 46 x 12 x 4 mm broad flat keys lock external side-wall seam lands during play. For storage, the same keys slide into authored recessed packed-lock lands spanning the two rim-to-rim trays; shoulders remain flush within the 210 x 190 mm packed XY envelope, so there are no additional projecting clips.
seam_keys_and_storage_locks.print_stance: Keys lie on their broad face; no support intended. Packed fit, key retention, and rattle are MAKE_PHYSICAL_VERIFY.
seam_keys_and_storage_locks.storage: Remove both bridge modules and both comet magazines; keep each pendulum captive under its keeper. On Tray A's active face, lay the two 110 x 64 x 14 mm bridges at local x=10..120 with y=10..74 and y=84..148, then lay the folded self-contained manual (maximum 180 x 100 x 3 mm) at x=10..190, y=10..110 over that 14 mm layer, for maximum Tray A stored height 17 mm. On Tray B, lay twelve comets flat in a 6 x 2 grid with centers x={25,56,87,118,149,180}, y={25,60}, for maximum height 5.5 mm; lay the two 72 x 38 x 8 mm magazines at x=10..82, y=90..128 and x=90..162, y=90..128. Opposed maximum stored heights total 25 mm inside the nominal 40 mm rim-defined cavity. Embossed placement outlines no higher than 0.3 mm mark these zones without interrupting trajectories. Exact fit, the eventual Release fold, closure, and rattle remain MAKE_PHYSICAL_VERIFY. Close trays rim-to-rim and install the two dual-use keys in their recessed packed-lock lands.

vaults.capture_interface: A comet scores only when its entire projected outline is beyond the embossed scoring plane and it rests flat inside one 38 mm-deep pocket. The 34 mm Narrow mouth gives 2 mm nominal lateral clearance per side around a 30 mm comet before printer compensation. Mouth edges receive 0.5 mm top chamfers but no raised floor lip. Vault geometry and actual retention are MAKE_PHYSICAL_VERIFY.
vaults.placement: The three mouths plus two 2.8 mm dividers are centered across the 170 mm field. Flanking inward lead walls connect the side rails to the outer vaults. The vault and eligible bank-facet geometry at the two physical ends is mirrored in world coordinates so each shooter sees the same shooter-relative order Medium/Wide/Narrow and the same target-end left/right facet pair. Scoring is identified by tactile pips, not an assumed color.

envelopes.field_coordinate_system: Use the left tray's inside end wall as x=0 and the opposite inside end wall as x=390, with the lapped tray seam centered at x=195. Vault pockets occupy x=0..38 and x=352..390, with scoring planes at x=38 and x=352. Clear launch bays occupy x=48..78 and x=312..342; shooter witness lines are the downfield bay edges x=78 and x=312. Gate center planes are x=145 and x=245, so each shooter encounters a near gate 67 mm after its witness line and a far gate 167 mm after its witness line. y=0 is the world-left inside wall and y=170 the world-right inside wall; shooter-relative left/right reverses at the opposite end.
envelopes.printer_bed_assumption: Each largest rigid part must fit within a 210 x 210 mm XY envelope. MAKE_PHYSICAL_VERIFY actual slicer extents, brim need, and packed closure.

interaction_character.agency: Each shot combines aim, launch position inside the bay, force, release cadence after pulsing, and direct-versus-bank intent. The fixed six pattern schedule prevents choosing only an easy gate state.
interaction_character.invitation: The READY stack is intended to cue taking one comet while the growing SPENT stack shows progress; paired arrows show where to pull; the hanging blades visibly fall; a single fingertip launches. The high rail and pipped vaults are intended to make the result readable from either end, PLAYTEST_VERIFY.
interaction_character.replay: A six-shot run is rules-bounded and designed for quick reset and comparison, PLAYTEST_VERIFY. The same field supports solo personal bests and rotationally mirrored competition without component changes.
interaction_character.surprise: A legal collision with a swinging blade may turn a direct shot into a late bank, while the three-ridge post-gate facets reward attempting to read that redirect. Actual redirect frequency and delight are PLAYTEST_VERIFY. No randomizer or hidden state is needed.

inventory.component: Dual-use side-seam slide keys / storage locks

deterministic_make_checks: Generate parametric source and STEP-first assembly; verify manifest, solids, dimensions, part count, wall thickness, and all named interfaces.

Slice every orientation under the declared printer/material/profile; report generated-support requirement, overhangs, first-layer footprint, bridges, and estimated material/time without claiming a print.
Check deployed and packed envelopes, tray seam surface delta target <=0.25 mm, comet/rail vertical containment, gate-end bypass denial, vault mouth widths, scoring planes, and inventory fit.

Compute gate clearance through the full stop-to-stop range, including blade-to-deck, blade-to-frame, trunnion-seat, keeper capture, bridge-foot sockets, and 30 mm comet pass/block envelopes. Assert the two end vault/facet fields are exact 180-degree rotational mirrors and all four bank facets lie beyond the correct far-gate plane for their shooting direction.
Verify rule geometry in CAD: at neutral both portal lanes exceed 30 mm; at each hard stop one lane is geometrically narrower than 30 mm and the other remains wider; no underside or end bypass exists.
physical_checks_required_before_performa: Print fit coupons for seam, slide key, gate foot, trunnion seat, keeper, and vault mouth before committing final clearances.

On the exact printed assembly, measure seam step, deck flatness, packed fit, gate floor clearance under warp, component mass, and wall retention under the declared 20 millijoule printed-fixture protocol plus observed legal human flicks.

Cycle each gate at least 100 times while checking free swing, trunnion/keeper damage, foot lift, rubbing, center-crossing count, oscillation duration, and reset time. The provisional usable target is at least three visible center crossings and at least 3 seconds after a full-stop release, not yet proven.

Run bounded low/medium/high flick trials for direct and bank intentions; record escapes, jams, gate bypasses, gate dislodgement, vault retention, and whether one person can pulse both gates before damping.
Inspect all printed parts before and after testing for sharp edges, fractures, tiny liberated fragments, and misleading tactile marks. None of these checks establishes regulatory certification.
quest_playtest: Create an executable event-level rules model with recorded PRNG seeds; do not pretend it simulates exact physical trajectories.

Run at least 1,000 complete two-player games across optimizing, exploratory, risk-seeking, bank-preferring, direct-preferring, and adversarial score-aware risk-selection policies. If the provisional named solo tiers remain in the artifact, also run at least 1,000 seeded solo runs; otherwise remove the tier names rather than claiming calibration.
Assert legality, termination, score set, maximum score, ordered gate dependency, bonus dependency, identical competitive pattern schedule, reset, bounded tiebreak, and trace completeness.

Measure first-shot/order effects, zero-shot and zero-round rates, ties, direct/bank choice dominance, vault choice dominance, policy separation, and provisional solo-tier attainment across perturbed shot-success assumptions.
Separately conduct human/physical evidence checks for teachability, launch comfort, state readability, fun, surprise, actual difficulty, and timing. Software evidence cannot answer those questions.

manufacturing_basis.edge_language: All touched and struck exterior edges use at least 1.0 mm fillets or chamfers where geometry permits; no needle points, knife edges, or decorative spines.
manufacturing_basis.material_assumption: PLA or PETG is a provisional material family only. Make must choose and declare one release material/profile and must not infer wear, impact strength, or safe cycle life from prose.
manufacturing_basis.print_stance_rule: Every separate part has a named broad flat stance and is intended to slice without generated support. Make must inspect the actual slicer rather than treating this intention as proof.
manufacturing_basis.process: Single-material consumer FFF, modeled parametrically and STEP-first during Make; nominal 0.4 mm nozzle and 0.20 mm layers.

product_definition.all_printable_boundary: Every game component is FFF-printed. Assembly uses only geometric seats, sliding keepers, and dovetail keys. Filament and access to a printer are manufacturing inputs, not included hardware.
product_definition.category: General-audience tabletop game; provisional intended age grade 14+ because it contains small launched parts. This is a design intent, not a regulatory determination.
product_definition.declared_round_length: Six shots per solo run; six mirrored waves, one shot per player per wave, in two-player play. Expected minutes are not claimed until timed Playtest.
product_definition.object: Portable analog tabletop dexterity game with disassemblable field, two moving gates, comet discs, integral scoring vaults, and self-storage.

common_shot_procedure: Take the next comet from the READY magazine, place it flat and wholly inside the launch bay behind its witness line, choose its starting position and aim, and announce ready. Accidental movement before ready is simply reset; after ready, touching the comet is allowed only for the one legal flick.

Use the next embossed pulse pattern. From the shooter's viewpoint, move the far gate blade to its indicated hard stop and release it, then move the near gate blade to its indicated hard stop and release it. Gate cadence is part of dexterity; gravity returns the blades but does not sustain their motion.

Begin exactly one forward flick with one bare fingertip while both blades visibly move and before the near blade completes its third crossing of the embossed center witness. Beginning the flick consumes the attempt whether the finger hits or misses the comet. If the launch window expires, or the player uses a second push, tool, blowing, table tilt, or post-ready hand contact other than the one flick, the comet is immediately dead for 0; there is no repulse or replay.
Only one comet is live. Side walls, fixed cheeks, moving blades, and marked bank facets are live rebound surfaces. A shot may touch either blade and continue if the gate remains seated.

The comet must first cross the near and far gate planes in that order and in the scoring direction through their bounded portals, then finish wholly beyond one target vault's scoring plane. A later backward or repeated crossing neither cancels nor re-credits an already legal forward clearance; any end, underside, or over-barrier bypass is dead. There are no points for partial gate progress.

A shot is dead for 0 immediately if it leaves the field, is touched after release, visibly jumps over a barrier, bypasses a gate around its end, lodges on top of a component, enters a home-side vault, or dislodges a gate or seam key. If a component detaches under an ordinary legal shot, stop play and record a mechanical failure rather than improvising a score.

After no visible comet movement for two seconds, score only its final target vault: Wide 2, Medium 4, Narrow 6. It must rest flat and wholly beyond one scoring plane inside one pocket; a leaning, wedged, touching, or straddling comet scores 0.

Add one 2-point Slingshot bonus if, after fully clearing the far gate and before entering the vault, the comet contacts exactly one of the current shooter's two eligible target-end three-ridge facets. Multiple contacts with that same facet add nothing; touching both eligible facets removes only the bonus. The opposite shooter's near-end facet pair is never eligible for this shot. Unclear contact receives no bonus.

Announce and record the score, place the used comet flat on the SPENT stack, wait for both blades to rest, and restore each bridge fully seated before the next pulse. Close or uncertain calls use the lower result.
rules_invariants_for_quest: Only per-shot scores 0, 2, 4, 6, or 8 are legal.
Any nonzero score implies ordered clearance of both gate planes and a wholly valid vault.
An 8 requires a Narrow vault plus exactly one valid post-far-gate facet condition; no partial or repeated bonus exists.
Both competitive players receive the same six shooter-relative pulse patterns and six shots.
The tiebreak terminates after three paired waves, so a match can end as a draw.
Simulation may model shot-event probabilities and policy choices but must never be described as physical friction, bounce, fit, safety, or human evidence.

solo.provisional_tiers: Cadet 10, Raider 18, and Master 26 are calibration targets only, not validated difficulty or player-response claims. Playtest must retain, revise, or remove them based on evidence.
solo.run: Take exactly six shots, one for each embossed pulse pattern, resetting the comet after every shot. Total the same vault and Slingshot scores; maximum is 48. Try to beat the prior recorded total, complete all three vault types in one run, or make two valid Slingshot heists in one run.
solo.setup: Use either six-comet set from one end, stacked flat in that end magazine's READY well. The opposite magazine remains empty.

two_player.round: Play six waves. In each wave, both players take one shot from their own end using the same shooter-relative pulse pattern; fully reset between shots. Each player therefore receives six shots and each pattern once.
two_player.setup: Players sit at opposite ends with one tactile comet set each. Choose the initial first player by agreement; if they do not agree, Sun-ridge shoots first. The other player shoots first in Wave 2 and first-shot order alternates every wave, giving each player three first and three second attempts.
two_player.ties: First compare number of valid Slingshot shots, then number of Narrow-vault successes. If still tied, play at most three mirrored sudden-death pairs using Pulse Patterns 1, 2, and 3 in that order. Before each pair, each player moves any one comet from the top of its SPENT stack back to READY; after its attempt it returns to SPENT, and sudden-death scores do not alter the completed regulation total or prior tie metrics. For each pair both players independently reset and pulse the same pattern, first shooter alternates, and higher single-shot score wins. If all three pairs tie, record a draw.
two_player.win: After Wave 6, higher total score wins. Maximum is 48 per player: six Narrow vaults with six valid Slingshot bonuses.

design_controls: One-finger direct flick only; no elastic, spring, catapult, compressed air, or thrown comet.

Twenty-millimeter side walls and inward lips are intended to retain a 5.5 mm high comet. Make must use a repeatable printed test fixture delivering 20 millijoules nominal horizontal impact energy to the comet from each launch extreme for at least 20 trials, plus observed legal human flicks; retention remains MAKE_PHYSICAL_VERIFY and the fixture is not a safety certification or proof against misuse.
All exposed tips and struck edges are rounded or chamfered; actual post-print sharp-edge inspection remains required.

Gate energy comes only from lifting a small printed pendulum. A 5 g mass at 29 mm effective radius released from 50 degrees is approximately 0.51 millijoule by m*g*L*(1-cos(theta)); this calculation is not a safety certification and actual mass/energy must be measured if used downstream.

Provisional age intent is 14+. Keep all comets and loose parts away from children under three and never aim at a person or animal. Release must make age and projectile warnings evidence-consistent rather than inferring compliance.
safety_and_use_boundaries.stop_conditions: Stop use if a trunnion, keeper, rail, bridge foot, comet, or tray cracks; if a gate rubs the floor; if a bridge lifts; or if any damaged part exposes a sharp edge. Replace the exact printed part before play.

selected_direction.core_reason: It makes gravity literal and inspectable: a player raises each blade, release converts gravitational potential to a decaying side-to-side oscillation, and that moving geometry directly changes the legal shot lane. The low finger flick and walled field avoid a catapult's stored-energy and airborne-shot emphasis. The same shot outcome supports fast solo and mirrored competitive rules.

materially_different_directions_consider.decision: Rejected for v1 because it adds stored-energy fatigue, airborne escape and eye-impact risk, support/tolerance sensitivity, and inconsistent launch energy. It would make the launcher dominate the gate-and-bank game.
materially_different_directions_consider.form: A flexure catapult lofts comets through vertical swinging hoops into cups.

materially_different_directions_consider.decision: Rejected because inertia rather than gravity sustains the useful motion, the lobes create floor pinch/jam zones, and print-in-place bearings would be clearance-sensitive. It reads less truthfully as a gravity gate.
materially_different_directions_consider.form: Horizontal lobed discs spin around vertical printed axles to expose changing windows in the field.

materially_different_directions_consider.decision: Retained only as a fallback if pendulum bridges fail physical verification. Rockers are compact and robust but have short travel, friction-dependent damping, and read as moving bumpers instead of gates to pass through.
materially_different_directions_consider.form: Self-righting curved obstacles rock when cocked or struck and redirect pucks.

materially_different_directions_consider.decision: Refined rather than selected intact. It strongly unifies gravity timing, routes, and vault decisions, but the incline couples gate torque to unwanted comet creep, makes the field naturally one-directional, adds shuttle kick and 42-part storage risks, uses smaller 18 mm comets plus loose washers/caps/tokens, and makes randomized loot obscure a fast mirrored skill comparison. Twin-Pulse preserves Leo's one-shot executable state, serial independently released gravity gates, route choice, bank play, and explicit Quest simulation while reducing the product to 24 larger, simpler printed pieces on a symmetric level field.
materially_different_directions_consider.form: Leo's specialist candidate uses a 7-degree split runway, three five-heading launch shuttles, two eccentric in-plane aperture bars, randomized loot tokens, and three vaults in a 42-piece inventory.

materially_different_directions_consider.decision: Selected because the mechanism is gravity-returned, visibly causal, low-energy, removable, inspectable, and compatible with flat support-free part orientations.
materially_different_directions_consider.form: Two removable bridges each carry a side-swing hanging blade that divides a bounded portal into alternating left and right lanes.

selected_direction.name: Twin-Pulse pendulum bridges

concept.summary: A portable, entirely FFF-printable tabletop dexterity game in which a player finger-flicks one low comet disc across a walled two-piece starfield, through two user-cocked side-swing gravity gates, and into 2-, 4-, or 6-point vaults. Each hanging gate blade oscillates left and right under gravity, alternately closing one lane and opening the other; legal blade contact is intended to permit redirects, subject to physical verification. A shot that clears both gates and then uses one eligible target-end rail facet before vaulting gains a 2-point slingshot bonus. Six rotationally mirrored pulse patterns are designed to give both players equivalent challenges, PLAYTEST_VERIFY, while the solo mode uses the same six-shot run as a compact personal-best heist. No spring, elastic, magnet, bearing, fastener, electronics, glue, or purchased hardware is required.
concept.title: Comet Heist: Twin-Pulse Vault Run

unresolved_risks.response: Prototype one removable gate first, tune open bearings and mass distribution, measure motion duration, then verify the two-gate shot ritual. If two gates remain unusable, seek a host-authorized concept revision rather than silently making a stationary gate claim.
unresolved_risks.risk: Pendulum damping or floor rub makes the second gate stop before launch.

unresolved_risks.response: Use seam/flatness coupons and recorded shot trials; revise surface orientation, joint, or field segmentation in Make while preserving the sealed interaction authority.
unresolved_risks.risk: Printed deck texture, seams, warp, or material creates inconsistent flicks and bank angles.

unresolved_risks.response: Run the declared 20 millijoule printed-fixture protocol and observed legal human launches; increase wall/lip containment or constrain the launch bay if retention fails. Do not add a spring launcher.
unresolved_risks.risk: Comets can jump the 20 mm walls under an ordinary legal flick.

unresolved_risks.response: Use fit coupons, broad roots, visible capture, and 100-cycle inspection; replace brittle geometry rather than claiming durability from CAD.
unresolved_risks.risk: Bridge feet, keeper, or integral trunnions loosen, jam, or fracture.

unresolved_risks.response: Use seeded event-model sweeps and exact physical/human trials. Adjust provisional mouth widths, scoring, or solo tiers only through evidence-bound downstream revision authority.
unresolved_risks.risk: The narrow vault or bank bonus dominates, or zeros make play frustrating.

unresolved_risks.response: The bounded exact-phrase search recorded no clear tabletop match but is not trademark clearance. Release must avoid a legal-clearance claim and rename if authoritative clearance later identifies a conflict.
unresolved_risks.risk: The name Comet Heist conflicts with an unlocated product or mark.

unresolved_risks.response: Maintain provisional 14+ positioning, retain low one-finger energy and high walls, inspect for liberated fragments, and include evidence-consistent warnings. No certification claim is authorized.
unresolved_risks.risk: Small launched discs and broken fragments present choking or eye-injury hazards.

claim_bindings.claim: FFF parts require orientation-aware overhang/support design, nozzle-aware feature thickness, and nonzero fit tolerances; no single clearance works for every printer/material.
claim_bindings.design_use: Use broad support-free stances, structural walls much thicker than one nominal extrusion, starting assembled motion clearance, fit coupons, and explicit slicer inspection.

claim_bindings.claim: Small parts and propelled objects require age-appropriate hazard consideration; projectile play can create eye injury and small components can create choking hazards.
claim_bindings.design_use: Use a provisional 14+ intent, low direct finger energy, rounded discs, high containment walls, no spring/elastic launcher, damage inspection, and truthful warnings without asserting compliance.

claim_bindings.claim: Flicked discs, obstacle contacts, bank-shot tactics, and firing discs through a slot are established dexterity-game elements.
claim_bindings.design_use: Do not claim those primitives as novel; distinguish the concept through two user-cocked gravity blades, ordered moving portals, fixed mirrored pulse sequence, post-gate bank condition, tactile vault risk, all-printed assembly, and solo parity.

design_calculations.calculation: For portal width 84 mm and blade width 14 mm, neutral gap on each side is (84-14)/2 = 35 mm. A 28.5 mm pivot radius at 50 degrees shifts the blade center about 21.8 mm, leaving about 13.2 mm on the closing side and 56.8 mm on the opening side. Relative to a 30 mm comet, one route is geometrically closed while the other is open at the stop. CAD must check the exact swept volumes.

For an illustrative 5 g pendulum, 29 mm effective radius, and 50-degree release, m*g*L*(1-cos(theta)) is approximately 0.00051 joule. Actual printed mass, center of mass, stops, impacts, and safety are unverified.
Six shots with a maximum per-shot score of Narrow 6 plus Slingshot 2 gives a rules maximum of 48. This is a deterministic rules bound, not an attainable-skill claim.

limitations: Manufacturer design guidance is a starting point, not proof that the exact CAD will slice or print on another machine/material.
Regulator pages motivate hazard controls but do not establish whether the finished product is a children's product, whether a warning is sufficient, or whether it complies with any standard.
No physical prototype, measured coefficient of friction, rebound model, pendulum duration, fatigue test, user observation, or completed game trace exists at Invent.
The event-level Quest simulation can test rule invariants and economy sensitivity only; it cannot validate actual trajectories or player dexterity.
Name and prior-art searches were bounded and non-exhaustive.
research.method: Bounded web research on 2026-08-27 used manufacturer and regulator primary sources for FFF and safety facts, plus publisher/product pages to map nearby dexterity mechanisms. Creative geometry, dimensions, rules, scoring, and target checks are explicitly labeled design decisions rather than sourced facts.

novelty_and_name_search.concept_boundary: Comet Heist does not claim invention of flicking, discs, vault targets, gates, or rebounds. Its authored combination is two removable gravity-returned moving lane blades crossed in order, identical shooter-relative pulse patterns, one-live-comet resolution, pipped risk-tier vaults, and a post-gate tactile bank condition in a clamshell all-printed field.
novelty_and_name_search.finding: The bounded search found nearby flick-disc, fixed-slot, obstacle, and bank-shot games but no clear exact-name tabletop product. Search incompleteness means this is neither patent nor trademark clearance and cannot support exclusivity claims.

sources.supports: FFF orientation/support limits, nozzle/perimeter scale, and the need for fit tolerance. The page states typical 45-60 degree clean overhangs, gives approximately 0.45 mm extrusion width for a common 0.4 mm nozzle, says zero-tolerance fits are not realistic, and offers at least 0.3 mm as an initial movable-part value while warning there is no universal clearance.
sources.title: Modeling with 3D printing in mind

sources.supports: Independent manufacturer guidance that minimum printable features depend on nozzle/settings, that sharp corners can warp, that bottom chamfers mitigate elephant foot, and that parts printed together need deliberate motion clearance. Its cited 0.6 mm printed-together gap is a reference, not proof for this separately assembled design.

sources.supports: CPSC warns that propelled objects can injure eyes and recommends protective design/age-appropriate use. It motivates low-energy, contained, no-sharp-point design but is not a product-specific certification.

sources.supports: Prior-art boundary: tabletop games already use flicked discs, obstacles, and creative bank shots. Those generic elements are not claimed as Comet Heist's novelty.
sources.title: Dexterity Game System

sources.supports: Prior-art boundary: a commercial two-player game already uses an elastic band to shoot discs through a fixed slot at speed. Comet Heist intentionally avoids elastics and differentiates with serial gravity-oscillating blades, ordered traversal, asymmetric vault risk, mirrored patterns, bank scoring, and solo play.
